confirmed.statement: The saved document is arXiv:2510.26490v1, dated 30 October 2025. All 470 markdown lines were read; the 16-page PDF ends with references and contains no appendix or participant-flow diagram.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, version stamp; pp. 1-16, complete document; pp. 14-16, References; all six embedded figures inspected.

confirmed.statement: S1 randomized 105 undergraduate people: 73 to the persona-guided interface and 32 to baseline ChatGPT, exactly as coded.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, section 4, Methodology, first paragraph.

confirmed.statement: The paper reports four participant exclusions followed by a final dataset of 101 conversation logs. Figure 6 independently labels participant-level originality with treatment n=70 and control n=31, totaling 101 analyzed people; this total does not count ideas, ratings, or output pairs.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 5, opening paragraph; pp. 9-10, section 5.3, participant portfolio centroids; p. 10, Figure 6, title, caption, and all bar labels.

confirmed.statement: The results text reports 69 treatment and 32 control logs, whereas Figure 6 reports 70 treatment and 31 control participants. Both total 101; the form accurately records the discrepancy and leaves both overall analyzed arm counts null.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 5, opening paragraph; p. 10, Figure 6, n labels above the treatment and control bars in each comparison.

confirmed.statement: The exclusion note is accurate: the stated total is four, but the listed reasons are minimal interaction n=1, inadequate duration n=2, timeout n=1, and authenticity n=1, summing to five reason assignments. The source does not explain overlap or resolve the discrepancy.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 5, first sentence; no reconciliation elsewhere in pp. 1-16.

confirmed.statement: Three additional people per arm were excluded specifically from survey analysis for incomplete questionnaires. From the prose arm counts, the derived survey counts are 69-3=66 and 32-3=29, consistent with the reported one-sample t-test degrees of freedom 65 and 28; these survey exclusions do not reduce the stated conversation-output total of 101.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, section 5, sentence spanning the page break; p. 6, forced-choice persona-preference paragraph, t(65) and t(28).

confirmed.statement: Taylor and Alex are switchable personas within the same treatment interface, not separately randomized human samples. The paper reports one experiment during one session; the survey, interaction, and creativity analyses use that experiment rather than independent studies whose Ns should be added.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, section 4, interface and condition descriptions; pp. 5-10, sections 5-5.3; p. 12, section 6.1, single-prompt, one-session limitation.

confirmed.statement: No fluency-specific or within-participant-distance sample counts are printed. Figure 6 does print 70/31 for participant-level originality; the form preserves those labels in the outcome description without treating them as an unambiguous overall arm split.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, section 5.3, Idea fluency paragraph; p. 10, Figure 6 and Within-participant idea diversity paragraph.

confirmed.statement: A further source inconsistency occurs in the behavioral analysis: section 5.2 prints treatment/control n=63/51 for divergent interactions and 59/51 for convergent interactions, although only 32 controls were randomized. The control n=51 is unexplained and does not establish additional unique people; these process counts are not coded as participant counts in the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, section 5.2, final paragraph; compare p. 4, section 4, randomized allocation and p. 5, section 5, retained sample.

confirmed.statement: No reuse of participants from another paper is disclosed. Cross-paper overlap remains unknown; the form makes no affirmative claim of an independent sample.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 1-16, complete document, especially pp. 4-5, Methodology, and pp. 14-16, References; form sample_overlap is blank.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds for S1 alone: 101 people are represented in the participant-level originality analysis of the randomized experiment, exceeding 50 without combining studies, repeated persona interactions, or multiple ideas per person.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, section 4, randomized allocation; p. 5, section 5, final dataset; p. 10, Figure 6, participant-level n=70 and n=31.

summary: The form correctly records 105 randomized and 101 analyzed people and leaves the conflicting analyzed arm counts unresolved. Criterion 2 holds for this single randomized study, despite the source inconsistencies documented in this check.
